First working paths, plus one application to start now

  • Supplier data: CJdropshipping. The app already searches CJ; add product detail, variants, stock by warehouse and freight quotes. At CJ you first install the free API app (Apps → Install App → Others → API), then add an API key (type API Key). Free; 1 request per second and a daily points budget, so one shared queue and caching.
  • Demand, free today: Google Trends CSVs you download, imported and labelled as imports (each export is scaled on its own, so never compared across files); your own stores' orders, the only real units-sold signal; Meta Ad Library for EU/UK ad activity after you confirm your identity.
  • Demand, apply now in parallel (approval required): Google Trends API (alpha). Built behind a switch that turns on when access arrives.
  • Paid option, only if you approve the spend: Keepa (Amazon sales-rank history and "bought in past month" ranges).

What each signal may honestly claim

  • Google Trends: relative search interest. Never volume, units or revenue.
  • CJ listed count and "trending" flag: popularity among CJ sellers, not shoppers.
  • AliExpress order counts: AliExpress-marketplace orders, window undefined.
  • Ad libraries: an ad exists and how long it ran (EU/UK). No spend for commercial ads.
  • Keepa / Amazon rank: rank within a category plus bracketed monthly sales.
  • Freight and stock: a quote at the time of the check, for that variant, destination and quantity.
  • Your store's orders: actual units, only for products you already sell.

What the designs assume, and what has to be built

  • Reused as is: the safe page fetcher (blocks internal addresses, caps redirects and size), store-scoped Knowledge Base retrieval and card ingestion, the agent run queue (a busy agent queues, never overwrites), approvals, budgets, encrypted credentials.
  • Extended: the agent registry allows one agent per store and role today, so "create a new Product Research agent" and per-agent model and effort are new fields on the same registry, not a second one.
  • New: store research profile (customers, price band, sourcing rules), supplier offers with variant and destination, demand observations with provenance, research tasks and history, pipeline stages, watchlists, comparison and unit economics.
